why_relevant: Albanian-language Kosovo portal with an economy desk that runs corporate and banking announcements. Adds redundancy to the weak-signal net: items missed or removed elsewhere often persist here.

Long-running Albanian-language outlet with a dedicated, directly addressable economy section listing page. Carries chamber-of-commerce, investment-law and banking-sector items, which frequently precede or accompany procurement activity.

Albanian-language analytical/commentary platform with substantive pieces on the Kosovo banking sector (ownership structure, foreign capital, crisis resilience). Not a news tripwire but a structural-context source that helps interpret why a given bank invests when it does.

A second sq-language economy-focused Kosovo portal distinct from Ekonomia Online. Small outlets like this one survive on corporate press releases, which is exactly the material — bank product launches, terminal rollouts, supplier partnerships — that this cell needs.

Aggregator/start page linking the full spread of Albanian-language Kosovo and diaspora outlets. Its outbound link list is a cheap way to enumerate second- and third-tier sq portals that no single search will surface, and to detect new entrants to the media landscape.

Commercial sq-language tender-alert aggregator for Kosovo. Not media, but it sits adjacent to this cell as the corroboration layer: when a media weak signal names a tender, this service (and its notice titles) is the fastest way to pin the contracting authority and lot. Also a pointer to which authorities and CPV areas are active.

Second sq-language commercial tender-monitoring service for Kosovo. Its existence and topic taxonomy are themselves intelligence about which procurement categories have a paying market; useful as a cross-check aggregator when a media item is ambiguous about which notice it refers to.

Commercial banks in Kosovo publish their own supplier calls and notices on 'Shpallje' pages. These are the private-sector analogue of a tender notice and are precisely the item a sq media report will echo. BKT's page is a confirmed instance; the same pattern should be enumerated across all licensed banks.

source_name: Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës (Kosovo Banking Association) as a media-named actor
why_relevant: The banking association is the recurring sq-language spokesperson for sector-wide payments and digitalisation initiatives; its media appearances point to which shared infrastructure projects (instant payments, card schemes, terminal standards) are moving. The Telegrafi tag page is a confirmed, directly pollable aggregation of those appearances.

source_name: e-Prokurimi / Elektronske javne nabavke Kosova (KRPP/ZRJN e-procurement platform, Serbian-language interface & legislation)
why_relevant: Kosovo's central e-procurement platform is the legally mandated publication point for tender notices, contract award notices and tender dossiers of ALL contracting authorities, including the Serb-majority municipalities (Severna Mitrovica, Zvecan, Zubin Potok, Leposavic, Gracanica, Strpce, Klokot, Ranilug, Partes, Novo Brdo). Kosovo's procurement law requires notices in Albanian, Serbian and English, so this is the single richest Serbian-language source for banking/payment-services awards. Confirmed Serbian-language secondary legislation is hosted at /HOME/Documents/Legislation/.../srb/.

source_name: Opstina Severna Mitrovica - Obavestenje za davanje ugovora (contract award notices, Serbian)
why_relevant: Official municipal site of the largest Serb-majority municipality, publishing contract award notices in Serbian directly - the buyer-side view of local contracts including any banking, treasury or payment-collection arrangements. Municipal-level notices often never surface in sq/en queries.

source_name: MAPL - Portal opstina (Ministry of Local Government Administration municipality portal, Serbian version)
why_relevant: Authoritative pointer/index giving the official website of every Kosovo municipality, including the Serb-majority ones, in Serbian. Snowball entry point to 10 municipal procurement sections; MAPL also publishes legality-review (shqyrtimi i ligjshmerise) pages per municipality that can expose contested municipal decisions incl. financial ones.

source_name: OSHP / Telo za razmatranje nabavki (Procurement Review Body), Serbian pages
why_relevant: Independent review body whose decisions on complaints re-open, annul or confirm awards. Its rulings name buyers, bidders, contract values and disqualification grounds - high-signal intelligence about who competes for banking/payment contracts and why awards fail. Serbian-language version exists.

source_name: Prokurimi Hapur / Otvorena nabavka (Open Procurement Kosovo), Serbian-Latin interface
why_relevant: Civil-society open-data mirror/analytics layer over Kosovo procurement, offering structured search of contracts by authority, supplier and value - far easier to query than the government portal, and available in Serbian Latin. Useful for building supplier maps of banks/payment vendors serving Serb-majority municipalities.

source_name: Kancelarija za Kosovo i Metohiju (Government of Serbia) - Javne nabavke
why_relevant: The core parallel-structure buyer: Serbia's Office for Kosovo and Metohija funds and procures for Serb-majority areas of Kosovo. Its procurement plans and notices reveal Serbia-side spending channels, and its treasury/bank account arrangements are the mechanism by which dinar-denominated salaries, pensions and social payments reach Kosovo Serbs - directly relevant to payments intelligence.

source_name: Portal javnih nabavki Republike Srbije (Serbian national e-procurement portal, UJN)
why_relevant: Where Serbia-side buyers operating for Kosovo (Kancelarija za KiM, Serbia-funded hospitals, schools, Postanska stedionica-serviced institutions, EPS Elektrokosmet) publish tenders and awards, including banking, treasury and payment-processing services. Invisible to Kosovo-portal-only monitoring and to sq/en queries.

Commercial tender-aggregation service that indexes Kosovo-region procurement notices in Serbian, including item-level records for buyers such as Kancelarija za Kosovo i Metohiju. Useful as a cross-check and as an early-warning feed where official portals are hard to scrape.

source_name: Centralna banka Republike Kosova (CBK/BQK) - Serbian-language site and payment-system pages
why_relevant: Regulator of banks and payment institutions operating in Kosovo, publishing regulations, licensing decisions and payment-system rules in Serbian. Decisive for the Serbian-language cell because CBK rulings (e.g. euro-only cash payments, dinar restrictions, licensing status of Serbian banks) determine what payment infrastructure is legal in Serb-majority municipalities; also a buyer of payment-system technology itself.

source_name: Narodna banka Srbije (NBS) - tenderi and Kosovo-related statements
why_relevant: NBS both procures (its own tenders, incl. payment/cash-handling technology) and issues authoritative Serbian-language statements on dinar circulation and payment operations in Kosovo - the parallel payment-system counterparty. Its Kosovo statements are the reference text most Serbian-language Kosovo media reproduce.

The leading independent Serbian-language news portal from North Kosovo. Reports in depth on bank branch closures (Komercijalna banka in Kosovska Mitrovica), licensing disputes, dinar/euro payment restrictions and municipal decisions - frequently the first and only public reporting on payment-infrastructure changes in Serb-majority areas. Also a snowball source for actor names and terminology.

Serbian-language broadcaster covering central-Kosovo Serb enclaves (Gracanica, Caglavica, Kosovo Polje). Covers local municipal decisions, enclave banking access and cash/payment problems that northern-focused outlets miss - complements KoSSev geographically.

Reported as the most-listened Serbian-language radio in Kosovo, based in Kosovska Mitrovica; publishes text news and podcasts on northern municipalities' administration, budgets and banking/currency issues. Its shared bylines with KoSSev/Kosovo Online/Radio Borzani make it a snowball hub for the Serbian-language media network.

Serbian-language web portal covering political, social and ECONOMIC issues from Kosovo, based in the Gracanica enclave. Economic desk makes it more likely than pure-news outlets to cover municipal contracts and banking access. Record here is the Media Ownership Monitor profile (ownership + own-site details); the outlet's own domain should be resolved from it rather than guessed.
